transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-10 14:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Alex, Priya, Miguel (Redwood) — Dana, Marcus, Sofia (Veridian)

Summary auto: quick check-in for the Private POC — focus on recent packet loss during peak, fallback routing, and next kernel plan.

00:00 Alex Choi: All right, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, agenda — quick status, logs/traces, kernel rollback debate, then next steps.
00:22 Dana Lerner: Thanks Alex. We're seeing intermittent 5–15% packet loss between the gateway and the inference pool on AZ-b during synthetic load. Happened twice yesterday afternoon.
00:40 Marcus Wynn: Note — we also observed a higher latency tail when a cross-AZ failover happened; it's like the path changes and MTU drops then fragments.
01:05 Priya Nair: mm-hmm, okay. Did you see any TCP retrans spikes or was it more UDP-ish? Our health checks are TCP but the model traffic is over TLS on 443 so retrans matters.
01:22 Marcus Wynn: Mostly TCP. Retrans and sockets in TIME_WAIT built up, we had to bump ephemeral port range.
01:50 Alex Choi: That's helpful. Can you confirm whether NAT gateway scaling was triggered? Sometimes a NAT autoscale causes transient SNAT table rebuilds and brief flow breaks.
02:12 Marcus Wynn: We already looked — NAT gateway shows no scale events in CloudWatch, but we do have a third-party virtual router in the mix for east-west. Could be that.
02:35 Sofia Ruiz: From security side, we want to avoid changing the egress proxy without an approved runbook. We need packet captures and a threat scan.
02:48 Miguel Torres: Understood. We'll put that as an action. Also, curious — has anyone tested fallback behavior to the hosted Redwood endpoint when private capacity becomes degraded?
03:05 Dana Lerner: We did a manual redirect once, but the latency jump was significant and a few sessions failed on re-auth. We don't have a graceful token handoff.
03:30 Priya Nair: Right, session continuity is hard. Our plan is to make fallback stateless by terminating long-lived KV caches for sessions tagged as ephemeral, so they can rehydrate on the hosted side. But that needs KV consistency checks.
03:55 Alex Choi: Okay, good. Let's zoom into the KV-cache persistence: Marcus, when you rebooted a node yesterday, did the kvcache restore happen cleanly? Any cache misses causing regen spikes?
04:20 Marcus Wynn: No, there were a bunch of cache-miss storms. The rebuild spiked token counts and we saw 2–3x per-token CPU.
04:45 Priya Nair: That points to the persistent volume mount timing or maybe the caching layer not honoring the fstab order during systemd startup. We'll add a start-order probe.
05:10 Dana Lerner: Also we saw NFS staleness warnings but it's a local SSD in our case — so might be driver related after the kernel patch.
05:30 Alex Choi: Good segue — kernel. The recent security patch we installed last week changed a network driver behavior that could impact offload and GRO. Priya, quick take?
05:50 Priya Nair: Yes, the patch forced a change in segmentation offload flags, which can cause fragmentation when combined with certain virtual routers. If that's the vector, we have two options: apply a micro-config to toggle offload flags or roll back the kernel to the previous release. Rollback is heavier, config toggle is lower risk but may impact throughput.
06:20 Sofia Ruiz: Security prefers patching; rollback is last resort. If we toggle offload we want a control plane mitigation to track degraded throughput.
06:40 Marcus Wynn: We can test toggling offload on one AZ and run the canary.
07:05 Alex Choi: Ok action — Marcus to toggle on a single subnet and run iperf + simulated inference load. Priya will stand up the benchmark harness.
07:25 Marcus Wynn: Yes, I'll do that. Also, we want to validate BGP session stability — we saw flaps on a third-party router.
07:40 Priya Nair: BGP flaps could be due to route reflection or keepalive timers. We should capture bgp adj logs and look for route withdrawals correlated with retrans spikes.
08:05 Dana Lerner: One odd thing — when the spike happens, the fallback route to hosted seems to add an extra hop via our transit VPC and we exceed the allowed egress bandwidth shaping. That causes queuing and drops.
08:30 Alex Choi: That suggests we need a blackhole-aware fallback: instead of routing all traffic to hosted, route only a proportion or degrade non-critical traffic. Our fallback policy supports percentage-based routing.
08:50 Miguel Torres: We can implement a 20% gradual shift for a canary phase so we avoid saturating the peering.
09:10 Sofia Ruiz: Please document the throttling policy. Compliance needs the audit trail for any cross-region data movement.
09:25 Alex Choi: Will do — we'll share an egress diagram and fallback policy doc.
09:40 Marcus Wynn: Regarding KV persistence, I found logs indicating slowfs mounts after ktimeouts. Could be an NVMe firmware mismatch with the kernel.
10:00 Priya Nair: Firmware mismatches can definitely cause I/O oddities. Can you share the NVMe firmware versions?
10:12 Marcus Wynn: Yep, including in the packet capture bundle.
10:25 Alex Choi: Good. On the canary benchmark — scope: 1 hour, 40 concurrent sessions, canary model gpt-small-001 (to simulate token rates), compare per-token latency and throughput between private pool and hosted fallback. Priya will run, Marcus will monitor network.
10:50 Priya Nair: We'll capture perf counters, tok throughput, and KV hit ratio. If rollback is needed, we can schedule a short maintenance window.
11:10 Dana Lerner: What are the rollback risks? If we rollback kernel, do we lose security fixes?
11:22 Priya Nair: Some patches are security-critical; rollback would re-open some vectors. We prefer toggling offload flags or applying a mitigative micro-patch from the distro.
11:40 Alex Choi: Understood. Let's keep rollback as contingency. If the micro-config fails in canary, then we'll take the rollback window with a full change advisory.
11:58 Miguel Torres: I'll prepare a rollback runbook with t-shirt sizing for risk and a post-mortem template.
12:15 Marcus Wynn: Another note — our auth tokens time out after 30s during region failover causing re-auth storms. Any guidance on graceful token exchange?
12:30 Alex Choi: We can increase short session lifetimes and add a handshake step that preserves a token reference so the hosted side can accept a reissued token. That requires minor API change and we'll provide a reference implementation.
12:52 Dana Lerner: Ok, that's helpful. We'll need a security review for that flow, Sofia to sign off.
13:05 Sofia Ruiz: Yep. Also please include SAML metadata flow in the appendix.
13:20 Alex Choi: We'll attach that. Now quick check on telemetry — are the tracer segments reaching Redwood console in time? We noticed traces lag by ~8s.
13:40 Marcus Wynn: The envoy sidecar is batching traces to reduce overhead; that's configured at 5s but spikes to 10s under load.
14:02 Priya Nair: We can tweak the tracer flush interval for the canary to 1s to get finer-grain telemetry while accepting a bit more overhead.
14:20 Miguel Torres: Ok, do that only for canary nodes.
14:35 Alex Choi: Great. Any blockers on the security docs?
14:45 Sofia Ruiz: Send KMS ARN for verification and include encryption in-transit diagram.
14:55 Alex Choi: Noted. We'll send the security appendix and egress diagram by Friday.
15:10 Marcus Wynn: About the NAT gateway suspicion — I dug deeper and found an ephemeral port exhaustion warning during the last incident window, even though autoscale didn't trigger — because our load balancer had lower idle timeout which kept ports open.
15:35 Priya Nair: That aligns with TIME_WAIT growth. Increasing idle timeout or using proxy protocol might help.
15:50 Dana Lerner: We prefer to adjust the load balancer first since it's the least intrusive.
16:05 Alex Choi: Agree. Marcus can try config tweak as a short-term mitigation while we run canary.
16:20 Marcus Wynn: I'll schedule that tonight in a maintenance window and report results.
16:35 Priya Nair: One final ask — can you also send the current quantization config and whether you used per-channel quant or block quant? We saw variance in token CPU when quant profiles mismatch.
16:55 Marcus Wynn: It's block-8 quant by default. We'll include the full model config.
17:10 Alex Choi: Perfect. To recap — actions: packet capture, canary benchmark, one-AZ offload toggle, LB idle timeout tweak, security docs. Schedule: benchmark 9/16, rollback window tentative 9/18.
17:40 Dana Lerner: That works. Thanks everyone.
17:50 Alex Choi: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the doc bundle and calendar invites for the canary and rollback window.
18:00 (meeting end)

Auto notes: Links shared during call: pilot-run-results.csv (link in chat), network-trace.zip (to be uploaded), security-appendix-v2.pdf (to be sent), canary-benchmark-dashboard (will be provisioned).

Transcript caveats: transcription contains occasional mis-hears — 'nvme' transcribed as 'N V M E' in places, some speaker labels merged.

Closing log: next sync after canary run or ad-hoc if kernel toggle fails.
